newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Diesel falls to 3-year lows, hits Asian refiners.
newsitem.headline: Diesel falls to 3-year lows, hits Asian refiners.

text.p: The slump in Asian diesel prices to three-year lows has hurt refiner's profit margins and little respite is seen for them near term due to poor regional demand, refiners and oil traders said on Thursday.

"The refiners are losing money because gas oil (diesel) prices have taken a big cut and the only way its going to improve is if there are more production cuts because demand looks pretty bad," a refining source said.

Diesel prices slumped on Wednesday below $20.00 per barrel -- the lowest level since 1994 -- after hitting a five-year high of $34.15 in December. One trader said prices could fall further, but were unlikely to go below $19.00.
Jet fuel prices slumped to less than $22.00, from a high of $33.00 in December.
The two products make up about 60 percent of a typical refinery's output.
Singapore refiners are currently losing about 50 cents for every barrel of Middle East crude refined in basic refining.
The Singapore refinery sector is Asia's swing producer and the key barometer despite producing only 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) of Asia's 18.1 million bpd.
Two refiners in Singapore have already cut output to try to improve profit margins, but traders said wider regional cut backs were needed to bolster the market.
Shell Singapore said it has cut output by 17 percent at its 435,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery. Industry sources said Esso Singapore has cut output by 10 percent at its 230,000-bpd refinery.
A Shell spokewoman said the cuts would continue until market conditions improved.
Singapore'sd two other refiners, Mobil Oil Singapore and Singapore Refining Co (SRC) were not expected to cut output because of internal company demands, sources said.
Industry sources said outside Singapore, South Korea could be next in line to cut output. The refinery sector is suffering suffering from reduced regional demand, especially from China.
South Korea -- with a 2.2 million bpd refining capacity -- has so far not made any production cuts. And historically it has tended to avoid cutting production.
The current weak price of products is not finding any major support from the already heavy loss of refinery production because of maintenance closures.

The International Energy Agency said planned Asian refinery maintenance shutdowns in Asia would lead to a loss in production of 1.02 million bpd in July, 960,000-bpd in August and 65,000-bpd in September.
But one trader said "I don't see the market bottoming yet. Unless China comes out to buy, margins will remain depressed."
A major facto behind the weak market conditions was the absence of buying from China. High stocks and weak domestic demand has prompted Chinese authorities to stop issuing import licences for now.
China produced 19.4819 million tonnes of diesel in the first five months, up 11.5 percent compared with the year-ago period, said a report by the State Statistical Bureau.
Chinese diesel imports in April were at about 380,000 tonne with Jan-April imports totalling at 2.4 million tonnes.
- - Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3093)
